title: Add one-shot prompt and persistent chat CLI modes
objective: Expose llm -p/--prompt as a strictly stateless one-shot completion mode and llm -c/--chat as a locally persisted chat-session mode with chat-id selection, validated rehydration, explicit LLM_CHAT_ID shell handoff, and backward-compatible request-file CLI behavior.

branch.name: wi-0010-cli-prompt-chat-sessions
branch.rationale: The repository workflow processes this feature as an ordered set of commits on the current branch; the intended work boundary is recorded without requiring a topic branch.

request.text: Expose features via easy CLI commands. Add llm -p/--prompt for a strictly one-off prompt that never creates, reads, mutates, resumes, or depends on chat-session history. Add llm -c/--chat <prompt> to always start a new chat session, create a chat ID when one is not supplied, persist chat state under /tmp/.llm/chat/{chat-id}.json, and provide the current chat ID through the documented LLM_CHAT_ID shell handoff. Subsequent separate llm <prompt> invocations use LLM_CHAT_ID to rehydrate the referenced valid chat JSON and continue that session. Add llm -c --chat-id <chat-id> <prompt> to always start a new session using the supplied identifier as its persistence destination; it must never resume existing state. Preserve the current config-file CLI. The first implementation task must refactor the existing CLI to use /home/michael/.cline/skills/nodejs-cli-pattern/SKILL.md because the current CLI does not use that pattern. No design task is required.

scope.name: cli-command-architecture
scope.description: Refactor the existing CLI into explicit argument, help, output, prompt-mode, and chat-mode boundaries following the required nodejs-cli-pattern guidance.
scope.reason: The current single-file argument switch must be made extensible before adding multiple modes.

scope.name: stateless-prompt-mode
scope.description: Add llm -p/--prompt as one completion invocation that never reads or writes chat-session state.
scope.reason: Users need a convenient one-off command without changing the current session or requiring session setup.

scope.name: persistent-chat-mode
scope.description: Add llm -c/--chat <prompt> as a fresh one-turn chat-session start with local JSON persistence under /tmp/.llm/chat/{chat-id}.json; only subsequent bare llm <prompt> invocations rehydrate the active session.
scope.reason: Users need multi-command conversation continuity across CLI processes.

scope.name: chat-id-and-environment
scope.description: Support fresh-session chat-ID creation or explicit --chat-id destination selection, environment-based continuation, validated JSON rehydration for subsequent bare prompts, and an honest shell environment handoff mechanism.
scope.reason: A process cannot mutate its parent shell environment, so the continuation contract must be explicit and testable.

scope.name: compatibility-and-safety
scope.description: Preserve positional/config-file behavior, existing help/version/debug behavior, safe exit codes, atomic session writes, restrictive file permissions, and bounded persisted data.
scope.reason: CLI additions must not break existing scripts or create an unsafe local state boundary.

nonGoals.name: prompt-session-isolation
nonGoals.description: Prompt mode must not create, read, mutate, resume, or depend on chat-session files or LLM_CHAT_ID.
nonGoals.reason: -p is explicitly a one-off operation and must not break or alter the current chat session.

nonGoals.name: remote-conversation-state
nonGoals.description: Do not depend on an OpenRouter conversation ID or server-side conversation persistence.
nonGoals.reason: OpenRouter is stateless for this use case; local history is authoritative.

nonGoals.name: arbitrary-command-execution
nonGoals.description: Do not add arbitrary shell tools, executable paths, JavaScript evaluation, or credential persistence to CLI chat state.
nonGoals.reason: The CLI must remain a bounded adapter over the existing provider/session library.

nonGoals.name: parent-environment-mutation-claim
nonGoals.description: Do not claim that a normal child-process invocation can mutate the invoking shell's environment.
nonGoals.reason: The implementation must use an explicit shell integration/export/handoff mechanism.

nonGoals.name: history-rewrite
nonGoals.description: Do not rewrite or amend immutable Git history.

nonGoals.name: interactive-repl
nonGoals.description: Do not implement a REPL, interactive chat loop, long-lived chat process, TTY requirement, readline prompt, stdin-driven message loop, or slash-command exit interface.
nonGoals.reason: Each CLI invocation handles one prompt and exits; persistence and the LLM_CHAT_ID handoff provide continuity across subsequent processes without requiring a terminal session.

nonGoals.name: chat-start-resume-confusion
nonGoals.description: Do not make llm -c resume an existing session. Every llm -c invocation starts a new session; --chat-id names the new session's persistence destination and does not select prior history.
nonGoals.reason: Continuation is deliberately a separate subsequent llm <prompt> invocation using the active LLM_CHAT_ID.

nonGoals.name: implicit-session-input
nonGoals.description: Do not make llm -c without a prompt wait for input or start an implicit session; the supported chat-start form is llm -c <prompt> or llm -c --chat-id <chat-id> <prompt>.
nonGoals.reason: The command boundary is one prompt per process and must remain usable from agents, scripts, pipes, and non-TTY environments.

items.name: cli-pattern-refactor
items.description: The existing CLI is refactored into the repository-approved nodejs-cli-pattern module boundaries before new prompt/chat behavior is added.
items.reason: The current src/cli.ts is a monolithic parser/executor and is not a maintainable base for multiple modes.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The first implementation task reads /home/michael/.cline/skills/nodejs-cli-pattern/SKILL.md and ports argument parsing, help, output, prompt execution, and chat execution into explicit native-ESM TypeScript modules with a thin CLI entrypoint.
Existing positional request-file, --config, --help, --version, --debug, exit-code, and JSON response behavior remains covered by automated regression tests.

items.name: stateless-prompt-command
items.description: llm -p/--prompt executes exactly one completion and never interacts with chat-session persistence.
items.reason: Prompt mode is a one-off convenience command and must not break or alter an active chat session.

acceptanceCriteria.description: llm -p <prompt> and llm --prompt <prompt> invoke one completion, return the assistant result, and support a machine-readable response option without creating or reading /tmp/.llm/chat files.
A test proves prompt mode does not consume, mutate, or replace LLM_CHAT_ID and does not modify an existing persisted chat session.

items.name: chat-session-persistence
items.description: llm -c/--chat <prompt> always starts a new local LlmChatSession, creates or uses a supplied chat ID, ignores any prior contents at that ID, and persists the fresh validated state under /tmp/.llm/chat/{chat-id}.json.
items.reason: Separate CLI processes need local conversation continuity.

acceptanceCriteria.description: llm -c <prompt> starts a new chat session, persists the initial context and accumulated provider-neutral history, and produces an identifier handoff for a subsequent invocation.

A subsequent session-mode llm <prompt> rehydrates the persisted session only when the environment handoff is present and the referenced JSON exists, is valid, and is within the approved session directory.
Session writes are atomic, use restrictive permissions, reject malformed or incompatible state, and do not persist credentials, raw provider diagnostics, or arbitrary executable content.

items.name: explicit-chat-id
items.description: llm -c --chat-id <chat-id> <prompt> selects a safe explicit identifier for a new session and never resumes existing state at that identifier.
items.reason: Users need deterministic session selection independent of the ambient environment.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every -c invocation starts with fresh history; --chat-id is used only as the new session's safe persistence identifier, never causes prior state to be loaded, and replaces the persisted state for that ID after the turn.

A supplied or generated safe identifier creates a new session under /tmp/.llm/chat/, while invalid identifiers such as traversal, separators, control characters, or oversized values are rejected before file access.

items.name: environment-handoff
items.description: The CLI provides an explicit, documented, and testable LLM_CHAT_ID shell handoff mechanism without falsely claiming child-process mutation of the parent shell environment.
items.reason: A normal executable cannot set an environment variable in its invoking shell, so the user-facing contract must be honest and usable.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The supported shell integration/export invocation makes the chat identifier available to subsequent llm <prompt> commands and is documented in help and public CLI guidance.

Without the required LLM_CHAT_ID handoff, a subsequent bare llm <prompt> continuation fails with a stable actionable error directing the user to start a fresh session with llm -c <prompt> or llm -c --chat-id <chat-id> <prompt>; prompt mode remains unaffected.

items.name: backward-compatible-cli-output
items.description: The existing config-file CLI remains compatible while prompt/chat modes provide deterministic human and machine-readable output, debug routing, one-prompt-per-process behavior, and stable exit codes.
items.reason: Existing scripts must not break when new command modes are added.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Existing request-file/config/help/version/debug invocations retain their current behavior and exit-code contract.
Each prompt/chat invocation exits after one provider turn without requiring a TTY or stdin loop, while user-facing output and debug diagnostics remain separated between stdout and stderr.

items.name: automated-evidence-and-conventions
items.description: The work follows the repository TypeScript/native-ESM/npm conventions and provides automated evidence for every requirement, invariant, security boundary, and non-goal.
items.reason: The feature crosses CLI parsing, filesystem persistence, public session state, docs, and generated declarations.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The ordered validation and review records report passing typecheck, tests, build, CLI command tests, persistence/security tests, declaration inspection, diff checks, conflict scans, and changed-path review.
The review task contains a data-driven automated coverage audit that fails if any requirement, acceptance criterion, invariant, test case, or verification obligation lacks executable evidence.
